Built for Google, not just for print

The magazine,
as real web pages

A PDF flipbook can’t be found by Google. The new site is built from the original InDesign files, so the same work that makes the magazine makes the website.

Step 01 — InDesign in

One file, once a month

Each edition is packaged from InDesign as usual. No re-typing listings, no second system for the family to learn or keep up.

Step 02 — Listings out

Price, town, beds, broker

Every listing is extracted as structured text — photo, price, beds & baths, acreage, town, description and tags like Price Reduced — not trapped inside a page image.

Step 03 — Found on Google

“Homes for sale in Ruidoso”

Each listing and town gets a clean, indexable page with proper real-estate schema, so a buyer searching from Texas or El Paso finds the Round-Up — not just a flipbook host.

Direction A — Modern Mountain

The new look, locked

Keep the name and the 25 years. Lose the yellow pages, red-and-blue banners and clip art. Colour pulled from the place itself — pine, brass, sand and rust.

Deep Pine#123528 · Primary
Forest#1E5A41 · Actions
Brass#D9A441 · Accent
Sand#E8DDD0 · Ground
Rust#B4552D · Otero / Alerts
Archivo Black
does the talking.

A bold grotesque wordmark and headlines — available on Google Fonts for the web and Adobe Fonts for InDesign, so print and web finally match. Prices set large and first, in the same face.

Labels — Uppercase · Wide-tracked · Brass
Data — IBM Plex Mono · Beds / Baths / Acres
Mark — Ridge-line in brass · No rope, no clip art
Photo — Full-bleed mountain & cabin · No panels
